label: Late original-phase input of b/e/0/w/g/m after a prefix rich in x/1/z/f/r/n-type tokens
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, never at the delimiter or during copying, and only at t>=3. The rate rises with position (orig_idx 5-8 have the highest rates; long sequences contribute most of the mass). It is gated by the current input token: b (strongest, 26% of mass), then e, 0, w, g, m, with weaker firing on z/o/q/a; it is essentially silent on other tokens. First occurrences of the token account for most activity (in_first=1 gives 91% of mass). Which earlier tokens appeared also matters: activation is much more likely when the prefix contains tokens like x, 1, z, f, r, n (first_tok x/1 have about 3x lift), and less likely after 2/3/u/w/o. Requiring 2 or more such prefix tokens raises dev precision from 0.16 to 0.30 while keeping 84% of activation mass. The history dependence looks like a graded weighted sum over the prefix rather than a crisp rule, so precision stays low; the top-quartile activations are the best covered (93% with the token+phase rule). Magnitude is highest on b/e/0 late in sequences with x/1-heavy prefixes.
